svg.text: File Storage Service (S3 / Dropbox style) — High-Level Architecture
control plane = thin lines through the API tier | data plane = thick red lines, bytes never touch your servers
control plane — small JSON, through the API tier
data plane — the bytes, bypassing the API tier
→ 1 PB/day ingest ⇒ dedup is survival, not polish
→ almost all must terminate at the CDN
ceiling is the METADATA DB, not storage —
Metadata DB — SQL, sharded by owner_id
IMMUTABLE versioned keys — new version = new key
multipart parts held durably until complete / abort
abort stale uploadIds (7d TTL) — you ARE billed for orphaned parts
presigned PUT / GET — bytes go client ↔ blob store directly, never through the API tier
Upload fails mid-transfer — resume path (part-based / S3 multipart)
server-side state: uploadId + set of completed parts · a part is ATOMIC — an interrupted PUT is discarded, never half-stored
persist each etag as it lands

If the client lost its local manifest (reinstall / new device): GET /uploads?contentHash=… → server's own pending rows. Never resumed? blob lifecycle aborts incomplete multipart uploads after ~7d (you ARE billed for orphaned parts) and GC drops the pending row.
Chunk size is a RESUME tradeoff, not just throughput: a dropped connection wastes one whole part — mobile-heavy clients argue for the 5 MB end.
Download fails mid-transfer — resume path (HTTP Range, RFC 7233)
NO server-side session — the partial lives entirely on the client; the server is stateless and unaware anything was in progress
WHY IMMUTABLE VERSIONED KEYS PAY OFF TWICE
bytes at a blobKey never change ⇒ If-Range can
NEVER mismatch ⇒ the 200-full-body path never fires
⇒ resume always succeeds, however long you were offline.
Same decision already removed object-store overwrite
pwrite() into a preallocated sparse file — beats one
window/RTT-limited TCP stream; each segment resumes
independently. Cost: 4× conns, more CDN pressure.
THE ASYMMETRY — upload resume is STATEFUL: the server holds durable partial state (uploadId + landed parts) and the client asks "what did you get?"
download resume is STATELESS: the client holds the partial state and tells the server "start from here", with If-Range guarding correctness.
